rv.q: Without knowing any better, one might easily mistake the new stage adaptation of Harper Lee's Pulitzer-winning 1960 novel 'A Mockingbird' for a revival of a classic Golden Age Broadway drama. So earnest in tone and full of plainspoken poetics...
TO KILL A MOCKINGBIRD still serves as a salutary reminder of the wrongs of the past and how much further things need to improve.
Sorkin's adaptation of Lee's important book is an excellent homage to its importance... it is as clever as it is painful, and there is no doubt it will stay with you for a long time.
